3_Result_Discussion: The high-precursor-concentration (1.6 mol/L) mixed-cation mixed-halide perovskite Cs0.1FA0.9Pb1I2.8Br0.2, where Cs⁺ stabilizes the α-phase and Br⁻ moderately widens the bandgap, was crystallized via a two-step spin-coating regimen (1000 rpm for 10 s, then 5000 rpm for 30 s) followed by a precisely timed chlorobenzene antisolvent drip (120 µL at 10 s) and a 110°C/15 min anneal, a process engineered to rapidly drive supersaturation, suppress heterogeneous nucleation, and promote dense, large-grained growth with minimal bulk defects and suppressed halide segregation. This optimized crystallization is directly corroborated by image-derived morphological evidence, which shows exceptional film continuity with 98.8% substrate coverage and a low average grayscale value of 10.6284, indicative of a uniform, pinhole-free morphology with reduced local defect density that ensures unimpeded charge transport pathways and minimizes non-radiative recombination centers. The resultant high-quality absorber layer, characterized by its excellent structural and interfacial integrity, enables efficient charge extraction and collection, yielding a champion device with a power conversion efficiency of 14.392%, supported by a high open-circuit voltage of 1.0127 V, a short-circuit current density of 18.961 mA/cm², and a fill factor of 74.955%.
